items.title: Kimberly-Clark Has Raised Its Dividend for 55 Straight Years. Here's How Much $10,000 Invested Pays Annually.
items.summary: Kimberly-Clark, a Dividend King with 55 consecutive years of dividend increases, offers investors a $10,000 stake generating approximately $471 annually in dividends with growth potential. The company recently completed its $49 billion acquisition of Kenvue, adding major brands like Listerine and Tylenol while targeting $1.9 billion in cost efficiencies over three years. Consumer staples stocks like KMB are gaining favor as alternatives to the vulnerable AI trade.

items.title: What's Wrong With Kimberly-Clark Stock?
items.summary: Kimberly-Clark's stock has significantly underperformed the S&P 500 over the past five years, dropping 16.5% while the index gained 56.5%. The company faces sluggish sales growth (1.7% on a comparable basis in 2025, declining further to -1.3% in Q3 2026), margin compression, and competitive pricing pressures. While the recent acquisition of Kenvue adds brands like Tylenol and Listerine, the integration risks are substantial given the company's already-challenged sales environment.

items.title: KMB Q3 Earnings Call Focuses on Kenvue Integration and Growth
items.summary: Kimberly-Clark (KMB) reported Q3 2026 adjusted earnings of $1.7 per share, beating estimates, though revenues declined 0.4% to $4.13B. The company completed its Kenvue acquisition and targets $1.9B in cost synergies. Management maintained its 2026 outlook despite headwinds from China disruptions, North American softness, and $250M in inflation. The company carries a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) rating.

items.title: Kimberly-Clark Q3 Earnings Beat on Lower Interest Costs, Sales Miss
items.summary: Kimberly-Clark reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.70, beating consensus estimates, but net sales declined 0.4% to $4.13 billion, missing expectations. The company faced headwinds from China social media disruptions, pricing pressures, and retail inventory movements. Adjusted operating profit fell 0.9%, while gross margins contracted 130 basis points. KMB completed its Kenvue acquisition and reaffirmed its 2026 standalone earnings outlook, though the stock has underperformed the industry significantly.

items.title: Kimberly-Clark vs. Coca-Cola: Which Dividend Stock Is the Better Buy Now?
items.summary: The article compares two defensive dividend stocks: Kimberly-Clark and Coca-Cola. While Kimberly-Clark offers a higher dividend yield (4.78%) and lower valuation multiples, Coca-Cola is recommended as the better buy due to superior profitability (27.3% net margin), stronger stock price appreciation (70.2% over 5 years), and consistent dividend growth (64 consecutive years of increases). Both are Dividend Kings with reliable payout histories.

items.title: Kimberly Clark is Down 20% From Its 52-Week High. Is the Dip Worth Buying?
items.summary: Kimberly Clark, a Dividend King with an attractive 5% yield, has fallen 20% from its 52-week high. However, the company faces significant headwinds including lowered full-year guidance, a major acquisition of Kenvue that will increase leverage, high dividend payout ratio of 85%, and underperformance compared to better-run competitors like Procter & Gamble. Only aggressive dividend investors should consider buying at current levels.

items.title: This Consumer Staples Giant's Dividend Streak Rivals PepsiCo. Nobody Talks About It.
items.summary: Kimberly-Clark is an overlooked Dividend King with a 54-year consecutive dividend increase streak matching PepsiCo's. Despite lower brand recognition, KMB offers a higher yield (4.7% vs 4.1%), more resilient demand for household products, and is acquiring Kenvue to enhance its global portfolio, making it an attractive option for income-focused investors.
